Chess Elo Prediction — v3¶

Multi-task neural network: BiLSTM with attention + static features + optional sequence autoencoder.

Key improvements over v2:

  • Time-control filter is off by default — the 600+0 filter was cutting 90%+ of games
  • Sequence autoencoder (AE): compress 120-move sequences to 32-d vectors offline, so the main training loop runs at static-feature speed
  • KL-divergence soft target inspired by the Ouzounis repo — model outputs a 40-bin rating distribution, not a single number
  • Elo-stratified WeightedRandomSampler — fixes the chronic under-representation of high-Elo games
  • Single-game inference cell at the bottom: paste any PGN and get a rating estimate
  • All heavy steps are cached to disk so you never recompute them

5 — Soft Distribution Targets (Ouzounis-style)¶

Rather than regressing to a single number, the model learns to output a probability distribution over 40 Elo buckets (each 100 points wide). The ground truth for each player is a Gaussian centred on their actual Elo with σ=200, then discretised into those buckets. This captures the fact that a player's single-game performance is noisy around their true rating.

Distribution for 1600: peak bin=1550,  recovered Elo=1600

7 — Sequence Autoencoder (optional but recommended on CPU)¶

The LSTM adds signal but is slow on CPU: a 200k-game run with USE_SEQUENTIAL=True takes hours. The autoencoder is the fix. We train it once, then use its encoder half to compress each game's move sequence into a AE_LATENT_DIM-dimensional vector and cache those vectors. The main model then just reads those cached vectors as extra static features — no recurrence at all during the main training loop.

Install requirement: pip install torch (already required). No extra package needed — the AE is a vanilla LSTM autoencoder built with PyTorch.

Set USE_AE = True in the Config cell to use this cell

9 — Model¶

Output head: when USE_DIST_TARGET=True the model predicts a 40-bin softmax distribution over rating ranges. Point estimate = weighted mean of that distribution. When False, direct Huber regression.

Trainable parameters: 1,354,481
